Hi Samir — great to meet you (and thanks for the details). Short answers up front: yes, we support EUR invoicing and EU data residency for hosted customers, and we have a few flexible pilot / minimum-spend paths depending on how you want to balance predictability vs. flexibility. Attached is our current EU rate card for hosted API (redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf) which shows list pricing and region-specific tiers.

Options we commonly use for pilots:
- Option A: Pure pay-as-you-go (no minimum). Good if you want zero commitment; price = list rate in the attachment.
- Option B: Short pilot credit + soft-monthly floor. Example: €5k pilot credit + a €3k/month floor if you convert to a month-to-month plan. This effectively guarantees capacity and gives you a predictable monthly cap while allowing an early exit within a short notice window.
- Option C: 3-month soft commit (discounted). Commit to a 3-month baseline (e.g., €9k total, invoiced monthly) and receive a 10–20% discount depending on band and usage mix.

Practical note: with your 50k tokens/day estimate we typically model two things — token volume (embedding + generation) and concurrency (peak QPS). I asked Karthik (cc'd) to add a couple of worked examples and a simple commit model so you can see how the math lands for EdgeAI.

Would you prefer the pilot invoiced in EUR or to receive a Redwood credit first and invoice the remainder later? Also happy to schedule a 30-min pricing walk-through this week.

Attachments: redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

Hi Samir — looping in specifics so you have concrete numbers to take to procurement. Below are a couple of simple scenarios using the usage profile Vanessa provided. Numbers are illustrative and can be refined after a short discovery call.

Assumptions:
- Avg 50k tokens/day => ~1.5M tokens/month
- Workload split: 70% generation, 30% embeddings (affects per-token effective rate)
- We price EU usage in EUR; VAT is applied per local rules and will appear on the invoice.

Scenario 1 — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- List blended rate (EU) ~ €0.0027 per token equivalent (i.e., €2.7 per 1k tokens)
- Estimated monthly bill: 1.5M tokens * €0.0027 = €4,050/month
- Pros: no minimum, fully elastic. Cons: no commit discounts and variable forecasting.

Scenario 2 — Pilot credit + soft floor (recommended for pilots)
- Pilot: €5,000 credit applied up front (covers initial usage and spikes).
- Soft monthly floor if converted: €3,000/month (below which we offer credit carry-forward for the pilot period).
- If you go month-to-month after pilot and average > floor, we reconcile usage vs. floor.
- Effective example: if you hit the estimated 1.5M tokens, base cost would be €4,050; with the €5k credit the first two months are largely covered. If you convert to the €3k/month soft floor, we’d offer a ~12% discount on blended rates for the commit band.

Scenario 3 — Short committed band (3 months)
- Commit band: €9k over 3 months (invoiced monthly at €3k)
- Discount: 15% off list blended rate for that band
- If usage materially exceeds the band, overage is billed at the discounted overage rate; if under, you keep remaining credit within the 3-month term.

A few operational notes:
- EU data residency: hosted EU region ensures data and KV cache remain in-region for the hosted offering.
- EUR invoicing: yes. We also support purchase orders and standard procurement paperwork; DocuSign links for SAs and MAs are straightforward.

I've attached a simple spreadsheet (proposed_commit_model.xlsx) with the above scenarios and a worked example for your 50k/day estimate. If you'd like, we can also produce a small 30–60 day mutual action plan (MAP) and an exportable pilot statement of work.

Attachments: proposed_commit_model.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

Thanks — happy to review on a quick call.
